episode.title: Venus: A Day Is LONGER Than Its Year

synopsis: Venus rotates so agonizingly slowly on its axis that a single day takes longer than its complete journey around the Sun.
narration: A single day on Venus lasts longer than its entire year around the Sun. Rotating in slow reverse, Venus takes two hundred forty days to turn once, causing the distant Sun to rise slowly in the west.

shots.prompt: A majestic panoramic view of yellow Venus shrouded in golden sulfuric clouds slowly revolving against the black backdrop of deep space.
Slow camera push down into the dense swirling amber cloud deck of Venus, showing light diffusing in reverse orientation across thick atmospheric layers.
Distant glare of the Sun appearing on the western atmospheric horizon of Venus as the planet imperceptibly spins, looping back to the full orbital scale view of shot one.

music: A rich atmospheric cosmic underscore driven by a slow steady mechanical synth pulse, swelling with warm synth brass chords as dense golden sulfur clouds illuminate in reverse rotation, sustaining a deep rhythmic drone that abruptly stops mid-phrase to allow an unbroken seamless loop.
